parsed.n_justification: The Salt River headwaters in Arizona's White Mountains span a strong elevation/vegetation gradient. Two columns capture the dominant control on water partitioning: a high-elevation mixed-conifer, snow-dominated site (major runoff source) and a lower-elevation ponderosa/pinyon-juniper site (evaporation-dominated). This isolates snow-driven vs ET-driven partitioning contrasts between the wet and dry years without over-fragmenting the single-column experiment.
requires_capabilities: single-column ELM (I-compset, satellite phenology or BGC)
DATM with GSWP3 or CRUNCEP forcing covering 1991-2003
surface dataset with site-appropriate PFT and soil texture
assumptions: Two full water years (Oct-Sep) 1993 and 2002 are the target contrast; 1991-1992 serve as spin-up/burn-in after cold-start.
1993 represents a wet El Nino year and 2002 the severe Southwest drought year in this region.
GSWP3/CRUNCEP reanalysis forcing adequately captures interannual precipitation contrast; no local bias-correction assumed.
Satellite-phenology (SP) mode used unless carbon-cycle feedbacks on transpiration are of interest, in which case BGC with prior accelerated-decomposition spin-up is substituted.
Columns are hydrologically independent (no lateral flow); results interpreted as point water balances, not routed streamflow.
PFLOTRAN coupling not required for this ET/runoff partitioning question and is omitted.
